review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact 4b82b66fa96f4bc3b93a10833dc75da1, its accepted claim/binding version 1, actual harness and plan, execution 97aac198d2bc4b10be4e3104e70bb614 and correlated monitor results. No correspondence issue found for the measured automatic-continuation proposition.

Applicability: JointImplicit assigns the zero-change proposal to Raft, whereas JointExplicit assigns it to the application. AutoLeave says to transition when possible. In the witnessed state node 1 remains an eligible leader, the implicit change is committed/applied, no transfer remains, and nodes 1 and 2 are a majority of both voter sets. The ordinary-proposal loss contract does not make unrelated client traffic a prerequisite of Raft-owned automatic work. No numeric deadline is inferred.

Legal entry and history: all nodes start from the same explicit configuration snapshot at index/term 1, with matching HardState and Applied=1, supported by NewRawNode's bootstrap guidance. The three actual RawNodes generate votes, entries and acknowledgments; the driver neither writes raft state nor forges support. It calls TransferLeader(3) serially during the leader's accepted Ready after the configuration entry has actually appeared in CommittedEntries and before ApplyConfChange/Advance. Ready/Advance does not prohibit serialized transfer while Ready is outstanding. The driver persists entries and HardState before any returned messages, applies only committed configuration entries in order and completes Advance after application. Voter 3 becomes unavailable at this point, with its traffic discarded; voter 2 and leader 1 continue ticking and processing every generated message and Ready. Learner 4 is absent in both control and transfer histories and is not required for either voter quorum. MemoryStorage substitutes completed durability, not protocol logic; no restart or physical durability claim follows.

Observation and identity: the prerequisite joint_committed is emitted for the actual entry before application; result fields and full retained state show that same entry subsequently applied. Identity is (scenario,joint_index), independent of the compared boolean, with admission Alias admitted. Monitor records match control result event 4 to prerequisite 0 and transfer result 10 to prerequisite 6. Both final result events are emitted regardless of stranded_cycle. The retained parsing_errors list is empty. Go's JSON output splits long state lines into chunks; reconstructing Output per test yielded complete CA_EVENT records and verified the fields rather than treating each chunk as a complete event.

Measured comparison: transfer admission is index 3, term 2, target 3. After application last=commit=applied=3, AutoLeave=true, outgoing count 3, no exit entry. At tick 10 target becomes 0. At ticks 20 and 30 full observed RawNode state repeats, work is drained, and ten actual heartbeat responses from voter 2 were consumed. Result stranded_cycle=true violates the independently stated no-stranded-automatic-work expectation. Control has exit index 4 applied, AutoLeave=false and stranded_cycle=false under the same unavailable-node fault. A later ordinary proposal occurs strictly after cycle_result and leads to exit index 5; it is recovery counterevidence, not an admission condition or a hidden completion substitute.

Recurrence correspondence: reflection recursively includes all scalar/collection protocol state in RawNode, raft, raftLog, unstable, readOnly, tracker including private sentCommit/inflight fields, and MemoryStorage entries/HardState/snapshot. It distinguishes nil and nonnil collections and compares canonical JSON strings without a hash. Function pointers tick/step are omitted, but the fixed source sets them from role transitions; the repeated role/term and the observed heartbeat-only paths do not change them. Log sinks and storage callStats do not choose protocol branches. Randomized election timeout values are included; global randomness is used only by resetRandomizedElectionTimeout, and the repeated leader/quorum and per-tick follower heartbeat path invokes no reset or election. The live queue is empty at both endpoints, storage/application work is drained, and the external scheduling rule repeats node 1 Tick, node 2 Tick and pump, with the unavailable-node policy fixed. Slice capacity and pointer alias identity are not serialized, but this cycle only produces/consumes heartbeat messages and does not mutate retained entries or membership, so these cannot enable a delayed exit. Driver diagnostic counters and loop index do not feed protocol calls within the repeated interval. Thus the ten-tick transition can recur under the same permitted live-quorum schedule; this is a finite recurring-state witness with sourced continuation, not a claim that thirty ticks alone proves eventual failure.

Cause and alternatives: appliedTo submits auto-exit but stepLeader drops it while leadTransferee is set. tickHeartbeat clears transfer without calling appliedTo or scheduling equivalent exit work. In the observed drained cycle no new committed application callback exists: leader beats only send heartbeats, follower heartbeats only commit the unchanged bounded index and respond, and leader responses refresh activity without appending new log work. A successful transfer, reelection or unrelated proposal can provide another application event. They explain recovery paths but do not invalidate the stable continuing-leader cycle. The observation establishes this local automatic-exit continuation defect, not consensus safety loss or a global client endpoint. A nonrecurring run would not prove general liveness; that limitation does not erase this complete recurring witness.
limitations: Synchronous RawNode and in-memory durability model; asynchronous storage and crash recovery are outside this execution.
Implicit learner addition retains identical incoming/outgoing voter sets; voter-removal availability consequences and client-visible outages are not measured.
The recurring schedule assumes node 3 remains unavailable while live voters continue; other schedules with a new leader or proposal can recover.
No general numeric liveness deadline or universal protocol proof is claimed.
